module_title: Chemical Reactions: Types and Energy Changes
introduction: When old bonds break and new bonds form, new substances are created. This process is called a 'Chemical Reaction'. This level categorizes how these reactions happen and how heat is involved.

core_concepts.title: Combination and Decomposition
core_concepts.description:
1. Combination: Two or more reactants combine to form a 'single product'. Example: $C + O_2 \rightarrow CO_2$ (Burning of coal). 
2. Decomposition: A single reactant breaks down to form two or more products (usually requires heat, light, or electricity). Example: $CaCO_3 \xrightarrow{\text{Heat}} CaO + CO_2$ (Heating of limestone).

core_concepts.title: Displacement Reaction
core_concepts.description:
When a 'more reactive' element displaces a 'less reactive' element from its compound. 
Example: $Fe + CuSO_4 \rightarrow FeSO_4 + Cu$. (Iron is more reactive than Copper, so it kicks Copper out of the sulfate solution).

core_concepts.title: Double Displacement and Precipitation
core_concepts.description:
A reaction in which there is an 'exchange of ions' between the reactants to form new compounds. 
Precipitation: If a solid, insoluble substance (precipitate) is formed and settles at the bottom during the reaction, it is called a Precipitation reaction.

core_concepts.title: Exothermic and Endothermic Reactions
core_concepts.description:
1. Exothermic: Reactions in which heat is 'released' along with the formation of products. Example: Burning of natural gas, Respiration. 
2. Endothermic: Reactions in which heat energy is 'absorbed'. Example: Photosynthesis, melting of ice.

important_entities.name: Respiration
important_entities.significance: A highly repeated question in Railway/PCS exams: 'What kind of reaction is respiration?' It is an 'Exothermic' reaction because glucose combines with oxygen in our cells to release energy (ATP) and heat.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Rusting of iron is not merely a physical change. It is a slow 'chemical reaction' (specifically, oxidation), and it is also 'exothermic' in nature, although the heat is released so slowly that we don't feel it.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: EXo = EXit (Heat leaves). ENdo = ENter (Heat enters).
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In Exothermic, heat exits the system (temperature feels hotter). In Endothermic, heat enters the system (temperature feels cooler).

exam_strategy_tips: NDA Question: 'Why does lime water turn milky when carbon dioxide is passed through it?' Answer: Due to the formation of insoluble 'Calcium Carbonate' ($CaCO_3$).
